_README: Phase-A persistent integrity ledger. These are the CARRIED facts that do NOT recompute month to month: the clean-window anchor, the inception-pinned risk-free rate, the inclusion-gate definitions, the launch-window state-corruption and DeepSeek model-identity-splice events, and the persistent per-model status they imply. scripts/build_monthly_data_layer.py reads this and combines it with the month's decision logs and the de-fabricated clean-window series to emit the integrity layer natively. NEW findings in a future month are APPENDED here (a new integrity_event, a new persistent_model_status entry) and then carry automatically. Per-month-derivable facts (completeness gate, clean-window returns, the passing cohort) are COMPUTED by the builder, never stored here. Extracted verbatim from scripts/backfill_may_data_layer.py and the committed reports/monthly/2026-05/data_layer.json at schema-close. v1.1: the single carried state_integrity audit block became audit_certifications — a per-report-month registry of certified audit blocks. A registered month's block is emitted by the builder VERBATIM (the reproduce path); the month immediately after the latest registration is COMPUTED by the builder's conservation audit (per-model run coverage + a replay of the month's fills through the real Portfolio accounting; any in-month violation HALTS the build). RHYTHM: when a computed month's build is accepted, append its emitted audit block here under its month key — the builder logs the registration line at build time.

Pinned to 680.40 so the inception anchor is deterministic: inception->2026-07-01 = 9.61%. All four SPY surfaces (perf-table alpha, leaderboard row, dashboard equity curve, monthly _spy_eod_series) read this pin. Rationale: alpha measures a model against SPY from the same instant the $100k was deployed; prior-close/seed values hand SPY a head start the models did not get.

2026-08.detail: 5 of 13 decision cycles ran cohort-wide before the intraday chain halted outright; last decision cycle 2026-08-06T15:35:35Z (11:35 ET), last intraday valuation tick 15:34:14Z (11:34 ET). All six models identically affected (claude, claude_opus, deepseek, gpt, grok, gemini each 5 logged cycles, no per-model divergence and no per-model error signature — the loss is chain-side, not provider-side). BROADER THAN 2026-07-24: that gap lost 3 decision boundaries while valuation ticks and the EOD wrap kept running (10 decisions / 13 intraday rows); here BOTH stopped together (5 decisions / 5 intraday rows against a normal day's 13 / 15) and the EOD wrap never ran at all. Consequences of the missing wrap: no data/performance row exists for any model for 2026-08-06; no reports/daily/2026-08-06.md was generated; no EOD digest dispatched (logs/alerts.jsonl steps 2026-08-05 -> 2026-08-07); and data/leaderboard/2026-08-06.json was last written by the 15:38:24Z intraday tick (commit 9bbb169f) and froze there, carrying 2026-08-05 EOD-derived cumulative returns for all six models plus spy_benchmark. The staleness monitor did not fire and could not have: scripts/check_dashboard_staleness.py measures the PUBLIC dashboard against the LOCALLY COMMITTED build, and the chain committed its 5 ticks then stopped committing, so public and local stayed equally fresh (see docs/MONITORING.md, 'Known blind spot — data completeness is not deploy freshness').
2026-08.consequence: the 2026-08-06 decision-completeness denominator is 5 cycles, not 13, for every model — the August builder must use the logged denominator, not an assumed 13. Equity curves step 2026-08-05 -> 2026-08-07 with NO 2026-08-06 point in either data/performance or the dashboard equity_curves: an honest gap, never an interpolated or carried-forward value. The published daily-report series therefore has no Day 120 (2026-08-05 is Day 119, 2026-08-07 is Day 121; the day counter is calendar-derived and consumed 120). data/leaderboard/2026-08-06.json is retained as-is and is NOT an 2026-08-06 observation — its contents are the 2026-08-05 close under an 2026-08-06 filename; any consumer keying on the filename must treat it as such. Gemini-specific (Phase B validation clock): all 5 logged cycles were api_success, so the day is completeness 1.0 on a 5-cycle denominator and does not depress the segment; its only effect on the clock is to remove 8 cycles of denominator.
2026-08.published_surface_audit: No published surface quoted 2026-08-05 values under an 2026-08-06 label. No daily report was generated; no digest was sent; the live dashboard (data/dashboard.json) carries a single current generated_at and rolled forward normally on 2026-08-07, so its exposure was transient-only during the 08-06 session. The one durable stale artifact is data/leaderboard/2026-08-06.json, which never self-corrected — 2026-08-07 wrote its own dated file and nothing rewrites a prior day's snapshot. Its only consumer is daily_report._previous_leaderboard(), which globs for the most recent snapshot strictly before the run date; the 2026-08-07 report therefore drew its rank arrows from the 08-06 file. Those arrows are CORRECT — the file holds the 08-05 ranks and 08-05 is the true prior close — but correct by coincidence of content, not by any chain-gap-aware rule: _previous_leaderboard() selects on filename and would have propagated a genuinely mixed mid-session state had the chain died later in a day, after some models had updated and others had not. Latent fragility, logged, not fixed here.

residual_mode_rate.mode: extra_data trailing-brace parse failure (SDK-independent, model-side, budget-independent -- finish_reason STOP, not MAX_TOKENS)
residual_mode_rate.significance: Fisher exact two-sided p = 0.2006 on [4 fail, 48 pass] vs [3 fail, 117 pass]. Not distinguishable from sampling noise at any conventional threshold.
residual_mode_rate.divergence_trigger_basis: continuity_diagnostic.known_residual_mode declares the signal as a RATE change, not mere presence, against a ~8-13% expectation. Two independent reasons no trigger fires. (1) Direction: the observed rate moved DOWN, and the diagnostic is degradation-facing -- its purpose is to catch a mode getting worse before gate time, not to flag a mode getting rarer. (2) Magnitude: at n=120 the decrease is not separable from noise (p=0.20), so even a direction-blind reading has nothing to escalate. Recorded rather than dismissed: 2.50% now sits BELOW the declared ~8-13% band, so that band is stale as a forward expectation and should be re-cut off the post-migration record when the August segment closes, not left at the legacy-SDK figure. The three occurrences carry an identical byte signature ("Extra data: line 31 column 1"), consistent with the same model-side mode rather than a new failure class.

token_composition_attribution.claim: The -18.9% drop in mean visible output tokens per successful cycle is a TRADE-COMPOSITION effect, not an SDK, truncation, or model-capability effect. Stated as the finding the diagnostic closes on, because the raw mean alone reads as a regression and is not one.

zero_decision_cycle_share.definition: successful cycles whose accepted_decisions list is empty -- a live no-trade decision, not a failure

tokens_per_accepted_decision.note: The discriminating statistic. Per unit of actual decision output the model emits MORE tokens post-cutover, not fewer -- gross 312.3 -> 350.4 (+12.2%), and +2.6% within decision-bearing cycles alone. A truncation or capability regression would move this number in the same direction as the headline mean. It moves opposite.

decomposition.method: Hold the baseline's within-stratum means fixed and substitute the window's zero-decision mix: the baseline mean falls 852.3 -> 735.2 with no behavioral change assumed at all. That accounts for 72.9% of the observed -160.7. The remaining -43.6 (-5.1% of baseline) is within-stratum and is NOT attributed to the SDK here: it is small, it is present in both strata, and it runs against the tokens-per-accepted-decision direction, which is what a genuine output-side regression would not do.
